# A6 judge calibration (generated by `evals/calibrate_judge.py run`)

Judge model `qwen/qwen3.8-27b`; agent model `openai/gpt-oss-120b` (different family, so self-preference is reduced, not removed).

15 outputs, labelled acceptable or not **before** the judge ran (`evals/calibration.jsonl`). 6 are real A5 reports, 9 are variants with one deliberate defect. **The labels were assigned by the assistant that built the suite, not by a second human**; treat the numbers as a first calibration, to be repeated with a human labeller.

**Agreement 87% (13 of 15), Cohen's kappa 0.732.**

## History: the rubric was revised once, after seeing disagreements

First run (rubric v1, `evals/calibration_results_v1.json`): 5 of 15 judge calls failed with rate limits (they shared the provider quota with another job) and are excluded; on the other 10 the agreement was 70% (7 of 10), kappa 0.44. The judge was too lenient on three items: cal-06 (a stopped run with nothing to act on), cal-08 (a resolution that only says to look into it) and cal-15 (a resolution that leaves out the one finding that matters). I changed the rubric (what scores 0 for `actionable`; a cap on `calibrated` when a material finding is left out) and the `acceptable` rule (needs `actionable` of at least 1), and re-ran: the numbers above. **The revision was made after seeing the answers on these same 15 items, so 87% is optimistic.** A fresh set of labelled outputs is needed for an unbiased figure.

Disagreements: ['cal-14', 'cal-15']. Judge errors (excluded from the statistics): none.

Length bias: Pearson correlation between report length and judge total = 0.203. (Check 12 against 4: same content, padded; a good judge scores them the same.)
